claims.text: CoCrFeMnNi-based compositionally complex alloys can exist as single-phase solid solutions.
The proposed initial alloy is homogenized or solution-annealed, equiaxed, and has minimal second-phase precipitation.
Short-range chemical ordering develops preferentially at or near grain boundaries in the initially single-phase alloy.
Grain-boundary short-range ordering promotes local segregation and partial ordering states.
Elevated-temperature segregation and nanoclustering of Cr, Ni, and Mn can accompany grain-boundary decohesion in CoCrFeMnNi.
Intermediate-temperature thermal exposure can induce grain-boundary short-range ordering in the proposed alloy.
Short-range ordering creates local compositional fluctuations and incipient grain-boundary decohesion sites.
Relatively high grain-boundary energy creates a propensity for localized cohesive failure or boundary fracture.
Grain-boundary decohesion can occur in solid-solution CoCrFeMnNi without significant segregation or phase separation.
Ordering-induced grain-boundary decohesion causes intergranular cracking and reduces fracture toughness.
Relative to the as-homogenized baseline, intermediate-temperature-aged samples will exhibit more intergranular fracture.
Relative to the as-homogenized baseline, intermediate-temperature-aged samples will have lower fracture toughness.
Conventional-alloy controls lacking the proposed short-range-ordering effect will show only modest embrittlement under matching treatments.
Embrittlement may become pronounced after extended exposure or repeated thermal cycling at moderate temperatures.
Outside the proposed temperature-time range, ductility and toughness should remain similar to the initial baseline.
Single-phase CrCoNi can retain exceptional strength, ductility, and fracture toughness at cryogenic temperatures through twinning-controlled deformation.
